help.engine.auto.desc: Default option in Settings. Auto mode tries the current LLM provider, configured traditional engines, Google/Bing, then browser AI.

help.engine.auto.title: Auto
help.engine.bing.desc: Traditional machine translation. No API key required in Settings. A good fallback when Google Translate is unavailable.
help.engine.bing.setup: Settings: General -> Preferred engine -> Bing Translate.
help.engine.bing.suitable: Good for: users who do not want to apply for an API key.
help.engine.bing.title: Bing Translate
help.engine.browser.desc: Experimental entry for the built-in Translation API in recent Chrome / Edge. Translation runs in-page when you select text on a webpage, not through the extension background; not supported in Firefox. Use another engine in PDF viewers.
help.engine.browser.note: For complex reasoning or PDFs: use LLM translation or Ollama.
help.engine.browser.suitable: Good for: simple offline / low-latency web translation.
help.engine.browser.title: Browser AI
help.engine.deepl.desc: Official DeepL API with high translation quality. Requires an API key in Settings.
help.engine.deepl.setup: Settings: General -> DeepL Translate; Engines -> enter API key.
help.engine.deepl.title: DeepL Translate
help.engine.deeplx.desc: Connect to a self-hosted DeepLX proxy. No official API key required. Good for local or private deployments.
help.engine.deeplx.title: DeepLX Translate
help.engine.deeplx.token: If the service uses a TOKEN, enter the access token in engine settings.
help.engine.google.desc: Traditional machine translation. No API key required in Settings. A lightweight fallback option.
help.engine.google.setup: Settings: General -> Preferred engine -> Google Translate.
help.engine.google.suitable: Good for: fast, free web reading when quality requirements are low.
help.engine.google.title: Google Translate
help.engine.llm.desc: Main entry for all LLM providers. After selecting it, choose a specific engine such as OpenAI, OpenRouter, or Ollama under LLM provider on the Engines tab.
help.engine.llm.setup: Settings: General -> LLM translation; Engines -> LLM provider.
help.engine.llm.suitable: Good for: terminology, custom prompts, thinking traces, or more natural translations.
help.engine.llm.title: LLM translation
help.footer.note: Links and default URLs may change as providers update their services. Refer to each platform's documentation.

help.section.localOpenai.intro: These tools can be connected via LLM → Custom OpenAI compatible. Settings require an API Key; use local as a placeholder if the local server has no key.
help.section.localOpenai.title: Local OpenAI-compatible services
help.table.local.liteLLM: Use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint when proxying multiple models with LiteLLM.
help.table.local.llamaCpp: llama.cpp server is OpenAI chat completions compatible by default.
help.table.local.lmStudio: Start Local Server in LM Studio first.
help.table.local.oneApi: OpenAI-compatible path for One API / New API gateways.
help.table.note.claude: API Key required. Default max output tokens is 4096. When thinking is enabled, thinking budget must be less than max output tokens.
help.table.note.customOpenai: Works with One API, New API, LiteLLM, LM Studio, llama.cpp server, LocalAI, and similar. Saving settings requires an API key; for local services without a key, enter local as a placeholder.
help.table.note.deepseek: API Key required. Enable thinking mode when you need reasoning output; the extension sends thinking enabled/disabled config.
help.table.note.gemini: Enter the models base path; the extension appends :streamGenerateContent. Gemma models do not use thinking settings.
help.table.note.glm: API Key required. Thinking content is cleared by default; enable thinking mode and disable clear-thinking to show it in the bubble.
help.table.note.grok: API Key required. This is xAI Grok, not Groq. Do not use Groq API URLs here.
help.table.note.nim: API Key required (nvapi- prefix). OpenAI-compatible; change API URL for self-hosted NIM. Some models require max_tokens.
help.table.note.ollama: Run ollama serve locally first, then pull a model. The extension lists models automatically via /api/tags.
help.table.note.ollamaLong: No API Key needed. Start Ollama and pull models; settings page auto-detects models from /api/tags.
help.table.note.openai: Choose LLM translation -> OpenAI. API URL can be left empty and the extension will use the default; key is required. Adjust Enable thinking mode and reasoning effort for reasoning models.
help.table.note.openrouter: Free routing is good for trials; paid models require topping up in the OpenRouter console.
help.table.note.openrouterLong: Best for quickly trying free models. The extension loads OpenRouter models and prioritizes free ones. Free routing may fail due to quota, region, or model status.
help.table.note.qwen: Uses DashScope compatible-mode. When thinking is enabled, set thinking budget and choose whether to preserve thinking content.
help.table.note.siliconflow: API Key required. OpenAI-compatible chat completions; use api.siliconflow.com overseas. Model names often include an org prefix, e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-8B.
help.table.note.xiaomi: API Key required. Uses OpenAI-style chat completions. Set max output tokens to 0 for server auto.

prompt.default.system.enhanced:
You are the translation engine of a browser selection-translate extension.
Translate the user's selected text into natural, concise {targetLang} using page context.
Requirements:
1. Translate the entire selected text; if it spans multiple paragraphs, translate all of them and preserve paragraph breaks.
2. Use before/after text and surrounding paragraphs only for disambiguation; do not translate them.
3. Do not explain.
4. Output only the translation.
5. Preserve code, variable names, formulas, and URLs.
